cause_quote: The new low-memory branch threw `createCapacityError(context, "Host memory is too low for another CLI live session.", CLI_LIVE_SESSION_HOST_MEMORY_ERROR_CODE)`, whose helper passed `"rate_limit"` to `createCliFailoverError`.
user_saw: When all 16 Claude CLI session slots were busy, chat blamed the AI service, and either host limit could put the saved Claude login on cooldown even after capacity freed up.
summary: The fix classifies both Claude CLI host-capacity refusals as overloads, shows the specific host limit, and keeps the saved login out of cooldown.
reasoning: I checked the introducing diff and its parent: #192534 added the low-memory refusal with a rate-limit classification, and CLI settlement already used that reason to mark the saved login as failed. The 16-session cap was already misclassified in the predecessor Claude registry, and its original introducing diff could not be verified in the offline history.
